subject: Civics
chapter_title: Grassroots Democracy – Part 3 (Local Government in Urban Areas)

keywords_and_definitions.definition: The official institution of local self-government managing civic affairs in an urban area.
The urban local body governing large metropolitan cities with high populations (Nagar Nigam).
The urban local body governing smaller towns and medium cities (Nagar Palika).
An administrative and electoral subdivision of a city or town.
An elected representative chosen by voters of a specific ward to advocate for local needs.
Senior civil administrative officer appointed by the State Government to execute city policies.
The elected political head and presiding officer of a Municipal Corporation.
A local tax levied on property owners serving as a primary revenue source for municipal services.

exhaustive_notes: 1. Types of Urban Local Bodies: Nagar Panchayat (transitional rural-to-urban), Municipal Council/Municipality (small/medium towns), Municipal Corporation (large cities).
2. Ward Administration: City divided into Wards; voters elect Ward Councillors. Ward Committees handle hyper-local grievances.
3. Political vs Administrative Leadership: Mayor (elected political head) vs Municipal Commissioner (state-appointed IAS administrative officer).
4. Essential Services: Sanitation, garbage collection, water supply, street lighting, road repair, public health, registration of births and deaths.
5. Revenue & Citizen Duty: Property tax, water tax, trade licenses, state grants. Active citizenship: domestic waste segregation.

2. What is an electoral subdivision of a city called?

short_answer_3_marks.question: 1. Distinguish between the roles of a Ward Councillor and a Municipal Commissioner.
short_answer_3_marks.answer: A Ward Councillor is an elected political representative who presents neighborhood issues, debates policies, and votes on municipal budgets. A Municipal Commissioner is an appointed senior civil servant who leads city administrative departments and executes council decisions.

long_answer_5_marks.question: 1. Describe the key functions and sources of revenue of an Urban Local Body.
long_answer_5_marks.answer:
Point-wise Answer:
1. Sanitation & Health: Waste collection, street sweeping, sewage maintenance, disease control.
2. Infrastructure: Clean drinking water supply, street lighting, road repairs, maintenance of public parks.
3. Civic Documentation: Official registration of births and deaths.
4. Internal Tax Revenue: Property tax, water tax, trade license fees, entertainment tax.
5. Government Grants: Financial grants allocated by State and Central Governments for major urban projects.

case_source_based_questions.source_passage: Urban waste management requires partnership between citizens and municipalities. When households segregate wet (biodegradable) and dry (recyclable) waste at home, municipal sanitation workers can process garbage efficiently, reducing landfill pollution.

questions.question: Q1. What simple household action makes municipal waste management efficient?
questions.answer: Segregating wet and dry waste at the domestic source.

questions.question: Q2. Why is waste segregation important for city environmental health?
questions.answer: It enables effective recycling and reduces toxic landfill pollution.
